play_name: Let real differences count, even when you love someone
behavioral_target: Pushing aside big differences, like values, faith, or future plans, because strong feelings feel more important.
trigger: You feel strong love for someone, and you also notice you two want different things in important areas.
old_play: You ignore the differences so you can keep loving them and keep the relationship going.
function_of_old_play: Ignoring the differences protects the good feelings for now. You do not have to face that you may not fit.
new_play: Let the differences be real. Name them plainly, even though you care. Then look at whether you both can truly live with them.
what_to_expect: It can hurt to admit that love may not be enough. You may feel loss or have to make a hard choice.
why_supports_task: You get an honest picture of what is true. That helps you accept what happened and stop loving past real facts.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Ignoring important differences because of strong feelings of love
context_limitations: Every couple has some differences. This is about not ignoring the big ones just because feelings are strong. If a difference is about your safety, take it seriously.
review_reason: Retrospective, past-tense wording; the alternative is a discernment-style derivation placed inside the Expiration/Acceptance task.
